options: Use all historical closure codes as the correct answers, since the large volume will average out individual errors
Let the agent label the historical tickets and use its labels as the answers
Skip evaluation and rely on engineers' feedback after launch
Have senior engineers adjudicate the correct cause on a representative sample and use that as ground truth
bank.explanation: Unreliable historical labels would make the test measure agreement with noise. An expert-adjudicated sample gives a trustworthy ground truth. Volume does not cancel systematic labelling errors, agent-generated labels are circular, and post-launch feedback alone is too late and unstructured.

bank.question: A vendor's contract for a packaged service-desk agent does not allow export of the configured prompts, tool definitions, knowledge index or interaction logs. Which risk does this create most directly?
options: Lock-in and lost evidence: switching means rebuilding, and past interactions cannot be investigated
Higher token usage per conversation, because the vendor's prompts cannot be optimised by the organisation's own team
Lower accuracy on technical questions
Reduced staff adoption in the first month
bank.explanation: Without portability of configuration and logs, the organisation cannot leave cleanly and may lose its audit trail. The clause does not affect token usage, accuracy or initial adoption.

bank.question: A bank runs its new account-opening agent in shadow mode for four weeks and it meets every quality threshold. What important question can shadow mode NOT answer on its own?
options: Whether the agent's outputs match the decisions experts would make on real, current account-opening cases
Whether the agent handles real-world document quality
How staff behave when actually relying on its output, such as over-trusting it
Whether its read-only look-ups work reliably against live systems
bank.explanation: In shadow mode outputs are compared but not used, so it tests quality on real inputs and live tool behaviour without customer impact. It cannot show how people work with the agent, which is why an assisted-mode stage follows.

bank.question: A bank processes 50,000 outgoing interbank payments a month. Errors are costly and hard to reverse once sent. How should agents be used in this process?
options: Give an agent bounded autonomy to release payments below USD 50,000, with a daily exceptions report
Use agents to prepare, pre-validate and flag payments, while release stays with existing controls
Avoid any AI involvement because payments are irreversible
Let an agent release payments but email a daily summary to operations
bank.explanation: High volume makes the process attractive, but irreversibility and impact keep release with existing controls. Agents add value upstream, catching errors before release. Autonomous release, even with summaries, puts irreversible actions in an agent's hands, while avoiding AI entirely forgoes safe value.

bank.question: Which claimed benefit in an agent business case is most likely to turn into real financial value?
options: 12,000 staff hours a year released, with no plan for how they will be used
An expected improvement in the organisation's innovation reputation
General improvements in staff morale from less repetitive work
Eight approved new posts for next year that will not need to be filled because the agent absorbs volume growth
bank.explanation: Avoiding approved hiring is a concrete, budgeted saving. Released hours without a plan, reputation and morale may be real but are hard to bank. Honest business cases separate bankable benefits from softer ones.

bank.question: The team designing an insurance endorsement agent learns that the rules for approving endorsements are not written down; two senior officers 'just know' them, and they sometimes disagree. What should happen before build?
options: Document the rules with the experts, resolve disagreements with the business owner, and build test cases
Let the agent infer the rules from past emails between the two officers
Build the agent now and let it learn the correct rules over time from production complaints and staff overrides
Ask each officer to train a separate agent with their own version of the rules
bank.explanation: Undocumented, inconsistent knowledge must be captured and agreed before an agent can apply it or be evaluated against it. Inferring rules from emails or complaints embeds the inconsistency, and two agents with conflicting rules institutionalise it.

bank.question: A retail bank in Dubai pilots a complaints agent in five branches during Ramadan and Eid, when complaint patterns and volumes change. Pilot branches show 20% faster resolution than the same branches in the previous quarter. What is the most reliable way to judge the agent's effect?
options: Accept the 20% improvement, since the same branches were compared
Extend the pilot until after Eid and then compare with the previous quarter again
Compare pilot branches with similar non-pilot branches over the same period
Ask branch managers to estimate how much of the improvement came from the agent
bank.explanation: A comparison group in the same period controls for seasonal effects that alter volumes and patterns. Comparing with a different quarter mixes the agent's effect with seasonality, and managers' estimates are not evidence.

bank.question: Which agent design has the highest exposure to indirect prompt injection leading to data theft?
options: An agent that summarises internal policy documents for staff and cannot send messages
One that reads customer emails, can look up any customer's account, and can email any address
An agent that reads public web pages for market news and writes a summary to an internal page, with no other tools or access
An agent that reads a customer's own uploaded documents and fills a form only that customer sees
bank.explanation: The email agent combines untrusted content, broad access to private data and unrestricted outbound communication, the full dangerous combination. Each of the other designs lacks at least one of those three conditions.

bank.question: A security tester shows that users can trick a bank's chat agent into revealing its system prompt. The prompt contains the agent's instructions and an API key for the complaints system. What is the most important lesson?
options: Add a stronger instruction never to reveal the prompt and close the finding
Switch to a model that is harder to trick, which removes the risk
Disable the chat channel permanently
Assume prompts can be exposed: remove secrets from prompts to a managed vault used by the tools, and rotate the exposed key
bank.explanation: System prompts should never hold secrets, because injection can reveal them. Credentials belong in a vault accessed by tools, and the exposed key must be rotated. Stronger instructions or models reduce but cannot eliminate disclosure, and closing the channel is disproportionate.

bank.question: An agent summarises customer complaints for a quality team using an external model provider. Each complaint record includes the full national ID number, account number and mobile number. The summaries never need these identifiers. What is the best control?
options: Mask or remove the identifiers before sending, keeping a case reference for traceability
Send the full records but add a contract clause asking the provider not to read or store any identifiers
Encrypt the summaries after they are produced
Only process complaints from customers who have not complained before
bank.explanation: Data minimisation means not sending what the task does not need; masking with a case reference keeps traceability. Asking a provider not to read data is not a control, encrypting the output does not protect the input, and filtering customers is irrelevant.

bank.question: Agent traces at a bank include customer names, account details and complaint text. The audit team wants them kept as long as possible; the data protection officer wants them deleted quickly. What is the best approach?
options: Delete traces after 24 hours to minimise privacy risk
Keep everything indefinitely in an open shared folder so auditors can find it
Set retention by record-keeping obligations and risk, protect traces with access control and encryption, and mask data not needed for investigation
Store traces only on the model provider's servers
bank.explanation: Traces must serve audit and investigation while respecting privacy, so retention follows obligations, access is restricted, and unnecessary data is masked. Immediate deletion destroys audit evidence, open indefinite storage violates privacy, and relying on the provider loses control.

bank.question: At 2 a.m., monitoring shows a customer-service agent's identity reading 20,000 customer records in 15 minutes, against a normal rate of about 300 an hour. What should the controls enable?
options: Nothing until the morning review, since agents are expected to run continuously and handle peak workloads
An automatic alert to on-call staff and the ability to pause the agent or tool at once
Deleting the agent's logs to protect the customer data
Raising the agent's rate limits to avoid errors
bank.explanation: Anomalous access needs rate alerts and a kill switch so the activity can be stopped, then investigated using the logs. Waiting allows a possible breach to continue, deleting logs destroys evidence, and raising limits helps an attacker.

bank.question: A customer asks why a digital lending agent declined to offer her a pre-approved limit. The team proposes sending her the model's step-by-step reasoning text as the explanation. What is the main problem?
options: Model reasoning text is not a guaranteed account of its output; explanations need documented criteria
The reasoning text is usually too short and too technical to be useful to a retail customer without editing
Customers are not entitled to any explanation about credit offers
The reasoning text would reveal the model provider's name
bank.explanation: Written reasoning is a helpful indication but not a reliable record of the true basis for an output. Decisions affecting customers should rest on documented criteria that a human can stand behind. Length and provider names are not the core issue, and fair treatment expectations favour explanation.

bank.question: A telecom operating in several countries plans an agent that will process customers' personal data. Which approach to data protection law is soundest when planning?
options: Apply only the rules of the country where the model provider is based, since that is where the processing physically happens
Apply the EU's GDPR everywhere and ignore national laws, since GDPR is the strictest model
Never let personal data leave the customer's home country, whatever the contracts or approvals
Design to shared principles such as minimisation and transfer safeguards, then confirm each country's law with compliance
bank.explanation: Data protection laws differ by country but share core principles, many modelled on the GDPR, so designing to those principles and confirming each jurisdiction's current rules is sound. The provider's location does not remove duties owed where customers are, GDPR does not replace national laws, and many laws allow transfers with safeguards rather than banning them outright.

bank.question: Using a three-tier risk model (low, medium, high), which use case should be classified as high risk?
options: An internal tool that drafts meeting agendas for staff to edit
An assistant that answers staff questions about the canteen menu and office timings
An agent that can adjust customers' loan repayment schedules within policy limits
A tool that summarises public news articles for the marketing team
bank.explanation: Changing a customer's contractual repayment terms affects customers financially and carries regulatory and fairness implications, making it high risk. The other uses are internal, low impact or involve public information.

bank.question: A bank's complaint agent suddenly starts producing longer replies and escalating less, although nobody changed its prompt or tools. Investigation shows the provider updated the model behind the same name. Which set of controls would have handled this best?
options: A larger budget for model usage and a faster internet connection
Contract terms requiring notice of model changes, using fixed model versions where offered, regression testing before adopting updates, and monitoring for behaviour shifts
A policy of never using external model providers
A stronger system prompt instructing the model never to change its behaviour
bank.explanation: Third-party model changes are managed through contracts, version control, regression tests and monitoring. Budget and bandwidth are irrelevant, a prompt cannot stop a provider's update, and avoiding all providers is rarely practical or necessary.

bank.question: A bank proposes an agent that recommends which SME loan applicants get fast-track review. Which governance requirement fits this use case best?
options: No specific requirements, because the agent only makes recommendations and a person still signs off every loan
Approval by the IT department only, since it is a technology project
Publishing the model's internal parameters to every applicant so that the scoring is fully transparent
Documented criteria, fairness testing by applicant group, human credit decisions and outcome monitoring
bank.explanation: Recommendations that shape who gets faster access to credit can create unfair outcomes, so they need documented criteria, fairness testing, human decisions and monitoring. Recommendation-only status does not remove risk, AI governance is not just an IT matter, and publishing parameters gives applicants nothing meaningful.

bank.question: The day before launch, a go-live review of a customer-facing agent finds one gap. Which gap should block launch?
options: There is no tested way to switch the agent off and revert to the manual process
The user guide has not yet been translated into French for internal staff
The project's lessons-learned document is still in draft
The agent's name has not been finalised by marketing
bank.explanation: A tested fallback and kill switch is essential before any customer-facing agent goes live; without it, an incident cannot be contained. The other gaps matter but can be closed shortly after launch without exposing customers to uncontained risk.

bank.question: A contact centre's service agent is targeted to reduce average handling time. Which paired KPI best prevents the agent from hitting the target in harmful ways?
options: Tokens used per conversation
Number of tools connected
Repeat-contact rate within seven days for the same issue
Number of prompt versions released
bank.explanation: An agent can cut handling time by rushing or closing unresolved issues; repeat contacts reveal that. Pairing metrics that pull against each other prevents gaming. Token use, tool counts and release counts do not reflect customer outcomes.

bank.question: An agent runs 50,000 tasks a month, each making 8 model calls at an average of USD 0.02 per call on a large model. The team routes 6 of the 8 calls (classification and extraction) to a smaller model costing USD 0.004 per call, with no quality loss. What is the new monthly model cost?
bank.explanation: Per task: 2 x 0.02 + 6 x 0.004 = USD 0.064. Monthly: 50,000 x 0.064 = USD 3,200, down from USD 8,000 (50,000 x 8 x 0.02). USD 4,800 is the saving, not the new cost, and USD 1,600 assumes every call moved.

bank.question: Two weeks after a telecom launches a new family bundle, sampled accuracy of its service agent drops from 95% to 84%, with errors concentrated on questions about the new bundle. What is the most likely root cause and lasting fix?
options: The model has become tired from handling high volumes; restart it every night to restore its accuracy
The provider has quietly degraded the underlying model, so the team should switch to a different provider at once to recover
Customers are asking harder questions in general, so the accuracy target should be lowered to match
Missing knowledge of the new bundle; make updating and testing agent content a step in the product-launch process
bank.explanation: Errors concentrated on a newly launched product point to missing knowledge. The lasting fix ties knowledge updates and testing into the product launch process. Models do not tire, the evidence does not implicate the provider, and lowering targets hides the problem.

bank.question: A bank needs completeness checks on 30,000 scanned account-opening forms each night, with results needed by 9 a.m. Which approach best balances cost and need?
options: A batch job overnight, a smaller model for extraction, and unclear forms escalated for review
Process each form in real time with the largest available model as soon as it is scanned, to maximise accuracy
Use a multi-agent debate on each form to maximise accuracy
Check only a 5% sample of forms to reduce cost
bank.explanation: Non-urgent, high-volume work suits batch processing, often at lower prices, with smaller models for routine extraction and humans for unclear cases. Real-time large-model processing and debates add cost without need, and sampling misses most incomplete forms.

bank.question: A bank's policy assistant keeps quoting a cash withdrawal limit that operations changed last month. Under a hub-and-spoke operating model, who should be accountable for preventing this?
options: The AI engineer who configured the assistant's prompts
The business data and knowledge owner responsible for keeping the policy content current
The model provider
The branch staff who asked the question
bank.explanation: Accuracy and currency of content belong to the business owner of that knowledge, supported by the platform's processes. Engineers manage configuration, not policy content, the provider has no knowledge of internal policies, and users are not responsible for the source.

bank.question: A bank trained 40 staff as agent builders and evaluators. Within a year, a third have left for technology firms offering better titles and pay. Which action most directly addresses this?
options: Stop training staff in AI skills to avoid losing them
Rely entirely on external consultants for all agent work
Create recognised career paths and roles, such as evaluation lead and agent product owner, with matching grades and progression
Require trained staff to sign agreements preventing them from ever working in technology
bank.explanation: New skills need recognised roles and progression, or the market will take the people you train. Stopping training or outsourcing everything leaves the bank without capability, and unreasonable restrictions are unlikely to be enforceable or good for morale.

bank.question: Monitoring shows a bank's service agent's sampled accuracy for card-dispute queries fell below the agreed 92% threshold for a week, while other query types remain above 95%. What does good practice require?
options: Switch off the whole agent until all query types are re-certified
Wait another month to see if accuracy recovers on its own
Lower the threshold for card-dispute queries to the current level
Move card-dispute queries to assisted mode, find and fix the root cause, add the failure cases to the regression set, and restore autonomy once re-tested
bank.explanation: Thresholds exist to trigger proportionate action on the affected request type, followed by root-cause fixes and regression tests that stop the problem returning. A full shutdown is disproportionate, waiting exposes customers, and lowering the threshold defeats its purpose.

bank.question: A customer service manager edits the live agent's prompt directly in production to make replies friendlier. Next day, the agent stops including mandatory disclosure text in some replies. What control failed?
options: Change control: prompt edits need versioning, regression testing and approval
Access control on the model provider's pricing page, which the manager should not have been able to view
The customer satisfaction survey design
The agent's long-term memory retention period
bank.explanation: A prompt edit changes system behaviour and can break unrelated requirements, so it must go through versioned release with regression tests. The other options have no bearing on an unreviewed production change.

bank.question: An agent has drafted vendor payment reminders at level 2 (human approval of each send) for five months. Which combination of evidence best supports moving this action to level 3?
options: Staff say they are tired of approving reminders, and the vendor recommends it
Approvers changed fewer than 1% of drafts over thousands of cases, monitoring is stable, reminders use approved templates and can be corrected, and the governance committee agrees
The agent has never caused a complaint, and a newer model version is available
The CEO has announced a target of full automation by year end
bank.explanation: Raising autonomy should rest on measured performance over enough volume, stable monitoring, low impact and reversibility, and governance approval. Staff fatigue, vendor advice, a new model, the absence of complaints or a top-down target are not evidence of safe performance.
